results.summary_before: This design implements an I2C slave port that can read and write the instruction memory of a RISC-V processor. It exposes four registers: one to set the memory address, one to read the current value, one to write a new value, and one unused register. The I2C interface uses external SDA and SCL pins, with an additional reset and chip-select input, and provides open-drain control for SDA. Testing requires an external I2C master to issue the documented read and write transactions.

results.summary_before: This is a multi-digit counter with configurable maximum values and carry-over behavior, built from modified 2-bit up/down counters. It supports two digits, with outputs serialized for 7-segment displays via external 8-bit shift registers such as the HC595. Operation requires three push buttons for digit control and limit refresh, plus three switches for mode selection, and it provides shift-clock outputs for the shift registers. The design is intended for educational use and includes no silicon test results.

results.summary_before: This project converts PS/2 keyboard input into Morse code output, supporting alphanumeric characters. It provides separate outputs for dits and dahs, a combined Morse output, and a 600Hz square wave for a buzzer. The design has two modes: one triggered by Enter and another by Space, and it generates Morse at approximately 15 WPM. Silicon testing confirmed it works at 1MHz, and it requires a PS/2 keyboard and an optional buzzer or speaker.
